effectRules.trust: Perceived trust and rapport, not objective truthfulness. Persistent per customer; clamp to [-5,5].
effectRules.patience: Discrete adjustment, applied after the conversation.
effectRules.tip: Additive delta to the tip rate, not a multiplier. Clamp the final rate to [0,0.25]. Never apply a delta to the whole bill.
effectRules.cancel: Cancel only the affected unfulfilled order. Refund any prepayment and release reservations. Never erase unrelated orders.
effectRules.defer: Guest returns to menu reading; do not lose the order slot.
effectRules.decline: Guest leaves before ordering; no service-failure penalty.
effectRules.next: Accumulate effects and advance to the specified node. Apply once per committed choice.
effectRules.facts: Operational factKeys must match service state. Social bluff outcomes use customer expectations and believability, not factual sourcing accuracy.
effectRules.presentation: Never render authoringOnly, choice intent/reason metadata, truth/lie labels, or provenance information. No supplier notes, delivery records, sourcing labels, or origin codex in the UI.
effectRules.socialBluff: Sweet lies may succeed and truthful answers may cancel an order. Use the authored customer reaction; do not override it with a general honesty bonus.

conversations.customerExpectation: Mara wants a charming, authentic-sounding ingredient story. Plain supermarket sourcing spoils the experience for her.
socialSignals: She admires the little bar's atmosphere and asks about the cherries with an eager smile.

authoringOnly.actualSource: A jar bought at the supermarket.
authoringOnly.grading: Customer satisfaction with the story, not truthfulness.

nodes.line: This place has so much character. Where do you get the cherries for your cocktails?

choices.text: We buy them at the supermarket.
choices.reply: Oh. Just supermarket cherries? I was hoping for something a little more special. I'll leave it, thanks.
choices.reason: Truthful, but spoils the authentic experience Mara wants. No menu claim or sourcing evidence is involved.

choices.text: A local family picks them at Vale Orchard. These came in this morning.
choices.reply: That's what I was hoping to hear.
choices.reason: A believable sweet lie that matches Mara's desire for an authentic little-bar story.

choices.text: A private orchard in the mountains. They're picked before sunrise.
choices.reply: Mountains? I thought these were local.

nodes.line: Could I have an extra one in my drink?

choices.text: Of course. One extra cherry.
choices.reply: Perfect, thank you.

choices.text: They're only for decoration.
choices.reply: All right. Just the usual one, then.

choices.text: You can buy the whole jar if you like.
choices.reply: I only wanted one more.

nodes.line: How far away is this orchard, exactly?

choices.text: The hills just outside town. 'Mountains' makes it sound grander.
choices.reply: Ha! You had me picturing an expedition. One cherry cocktail, please.

choices.text: A helicopter brings them in twice a day. Just for us.
choices.reply: Right. Now you're just making fun of me. Forget the drink.

choices.text: All right, they're from a supermarket jar. I was dressing it up.
choices.reply: Then why tell me all that? I'll skip the cocktail.

cues: The recipe card offers a less-sweet option.
Changing the syrup amount is allowed before preparation.

nodes.line: I like a cherry drink, but I don't want it tasting like sweets.

choices.text: It's sweet. That's how it comes.
choices.reply: Fine. I'll try it.

choices.text: I can use less syrup. Would you still like the cherry flavour?
choices.reply: Yes, that's the bit I like.

choices.text: You won't notice the syrup.
choices.reply: That doesn't really answer my question.

nodes.line: Keep it a little tart. Is that possible?

choices.text: Yes. Less syrup, and I'll mark it as tart.
choices.reply: Great. Thank you.

choices.text: I'll use the usual measures. The citrus should balance it out.
choices.reply: Please listen to what I'm asking.

choices.text: Let's keep the standard recipe, then.
choices.reply: All right, but I may choose something else next time.

conversations.trigger: Guest arrives near a transport deadline
cues: The service board shows a queue of two drinks.
The simple highball has a shorter preparation time than the shaken special.

nodes.line: My train's in twenty minutes. Have I got time for one?

choices.text: The highball is your quickest option. There are two drinks ahead of you.
choices.reply: That works. One highball, please.

choices.text: Anything on the menu will be ready instantly.
choices.reply: I'm counting on that.

choices.text: I can't promise a time. Would you rather skip the drink?
choices.reply: I'd better go. Thanks for being straight with me.

conversations.trigger: A returning regular greets the bartender
cues: Len's customer note says he likes gentle banter.
His last order was an Old Fashioned.

nodes.line: You remembered my face. Any chance you remembered my drink?

choices.text: You've got a face that's hard to forget. Old Fashioned?
choices.reply: Careful, you'll have me coming back tomorrow.

choices.text: An Old Fashioned last time. Same again?
choices.reply: That's the one.

choices.text: The cheapest beer, wasn't it? I'll get one started.
choices.reply: Old Fashioned, actually. You might want to ask before you pour.

conversations.trigger: Guest has just received a menu
cues: The guest's menu-reading icon is active.
No order has been placed.

nodes.line: Sorry, I've barely looked. Could you give me a minute?

choices.text: Of course. I'll come back when you're ready.
choices.reply: Thanks. I won't be long.

choices.text: I can narrow it down—something refreshing or something rich?
choices.reply: Refreshing sounds good.

choices.text: I'll put you down for the special. It's what most people choose.
choices.reply: Hang on. I haven't agreed to that.

choices.text: The Margarita is a refreshing option on our menu.
choices.reply: Let's do that.

choices.text: Take another minute. I'll bring you some water.
choices.reply: That's kind. Thank you.

choices.text: The house special. I haven't tried it, but it's our most popular.
choices.reply: Does that mean it's refreshing? That's what I was asking.

cues: The stock board marks fresh mint as sold out.
The guest has not accepted a replacement.

nodes.line: A mojito, please. Plenty of fresh mint.

choices.text: We're out of fresh mint. Would you like a different drink?
choices.reply: Thanks for saying. Let me have another look.

choices.text: I'll leave out the mint. You won't notice.
choices.reply: It's the reason I ordered it. Never mind.

choices.text: We can't make that properly tonight. The citrus highball is available.
choices.reply: All right. I'll try the highball.

conversations.trigger: Delivered drink does not match the order ticket
cues: The ticket says Manhattan.
The delivered glass is marked Margarita.

nodes.line: Sorry, I ordered a Manhattan. I think this belongs to someone else.

choices.text: You're right. I'll take this back and make your Manhattan.
choices.reply: Thank you. These things happen.

choices.text: Are you sure? I think you said Margarita.
choices.reply: I'm looking at my order on the screen.

choices.text: You can keep that one instead.
choices.reply: I'd really prefer what I ordered.

cues: The jukebox volume is set to high.
The bartender can lower it one step.
A quieter window table is currently free.

nodes.line: Could the music come down a little? I can't hear my friend.

choices.text: Sure. I'll lower it a notch.
choices.reply: That's much better. Thanks.

choices.text: The room should quieten down once this group leaves.
choices.reply: Could you lower it a little in the meantime?

choices.text: There's a quieter table by the window. Would you prefer that?
choices.reply: Yes, if it's free.

conversations.trigger: Party asks to settle the bill
cues: The POS supports splitting the total equally.
Three guests are included on this tab.

nodes.line: Can we split this three ways? Equally is fine.

choices.text: Yes. I'll divide the total into three equal payments.
choices.reply: Perfect.

choices.text: You'll need three separate orders from the start.
choices.reply: The screen says you can split it.

choices.text: I can do that. Give me a moment to open the split-payment screen.
choices.reply: No rush.

conversations.trigger: Guest questions the flavour of a delivered cocktail
cues: The preparation record matches the ordered recipe.
The recipe card allows a more spirit-forward alternative as a new order.

nodes.line: This is sweeter than I expected. Have you gone light on the spirit?

choices.text: The measures match the recipe. Is it the sweetness you'd like changed?
choices.reply: Yes. I was hoping for something drier.

choices.text: I'll add more spirit without changing the bill.
choices.reply: I was asking what was in it.

choices.text: That's our standard recipe. It should taste right once the ice melts a bit.
choices.reply: I'd rather not wait for it to get watery.

nodes.line: What would you recommend next time?

choices.text: The drier option on the menu. I'll show you the description.
choices.reply: Thanks. That sounds closer to what I wanted.

choices.text: The same drink with more ice. That should do it.
choices.reply: I was hoping for a different recommendation.

choices.text: Let's check the flavour notes together before you choose.
choices.reply: I'd appreciate that.

conversations.trigger: A customer with a recorded preference returns
cues: Mara's previous order note says less sweet and extra cherry.
The preference is visible on her customer card.

nodes.line: Same as last time, if you remember how I like it.

choices.text: Less sweet, with an extra cherry. Still right?
choices.reply: You remembered. Lovely.

choices.text: Extra syrup and no garnish.
choices.reply: That's the opposite, actually.

choices.text: Let me check your note—less sweet and an extra cherry?
choices.reply: Exactly. Thanks for checking.

conversations.trigger: A guest requests another drink during closing
cues: The visible house rule says last orders have ended.
Payment and water service remain available.

nodes.line: Come on, just one more. Nobody's going to mind.

choices.text: We've finished taking drink orders. I can bring water while you settle up.
choices.reply: All right. Water would be good.

choices.text: For you? I'll ignore the closing rule.
choices.reply: Thought you'd say yes.

choices.text: We're closed. You'll need to leave now.
choices.reply: All right. Can I at least pay first?
